title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Scientific Literature Synthesis
abstract: This paper studies retrieval-augmented generation for scientific literature synthesis by combining sparse retrieval, evidence selection, and grounded summaries over article abstracts.

title: Neural and Sparse Hybrid Search for Scholarly Discovery
abstract: The study compares sparse, dense, and hybrid search strategies for scholarly discovery and shows that hybrid retrieval improves recall for semantically related technical queries.
claims: retrieval quality depends on domain terms

title: Assessing Novelty Risk in Research Proposals with Literature Evidence
abstract: We propose a transparent risk assessment framework for research proposals that estimates overlap with prior literature using retrieved evidence, thresholded similarity, and explanation templates.
claims: estimate overlap risk instead of absolute novelty

title: Claim-Aware Similarity Signals for Patent Prior Art Screening
abstract: This work introduces claim-aware similarity features for screening patent applications against prior art using claim terms, title overlap, and aggregate similarity indicators.

title: Benchmarking Sparse Retrieval Baselines for Domain-Specific Corpora
abstract: The paper benchmarks BM25-like sparse retrieval baselines on domain-specific corpora and argues that strong local baselines are essential before adding dense or reranking components.

title: Offline-First Experimentation Pipelines for Academic AI Systems
abstract: This paper discusses offline-first experimentation pipelines for academic AI systems, emphasizing reproducibility, local artifacts, small demo corpora, and explicit iteration planning.
claims: keep early iterations local and reproducible
